problem: The simplified model F = T/(nr) assumes every arm shares the torque equally. With a cast rim that flexes, the arms near the loaded side take most of the torque, so many textbooks design integral arms for the whole torque shared by only half the arms, giving M = 2T/n. A student using F = T/(nr) alone may under-design the arms.
fix: Add a note: 'In practice a cast rim is not rigid, so only about half the arms can be assumed to share the torque. Designers then take M = 2T/n. The formula M = T/n above is the ideal equal-sharing case.'

problem: The text tells the student to 'check σt = Fc/A', but σt is never defined and A appears in the legend attached to a formula block that does not contain σt.
fix: Define it in the legend: 'σt = Fc/A is the direct tensile stress in the arm in Pa, with A the arm cross-section area in m².'
